KEEP THE DETAILS TOGETHER

Dispute resolution policy

A clear process for raising a concern, preserving useful records and working towards a fair resolution between couples, suppliers and WedSparks.

Prepared for review · 18 October 2026 · Not yet effective. Business identity, contact details and operational rules require confirmation.

1. Scope and status2. Urgent concerns3. Start with a clear written account4. Keep relevant evidence5. Describe the remedy sought6. Escalating to WedSparks7. Fair participation and written outcomes8. Card and payment-provider disputes9. External options and account action10. Records, learning and changes

1. Scope and status

Review draft dated 18 October 2026. This policy covers concerns about supplier services, platform services, invoices, payments, credits and account activity. It should be read with the Platform Terms and Cancellations and Refunds Policy. Final support details, case handling responsibilities and response targets must be confirmed before publication.

WedSparks can help organise records and facilitate communication within its actual capabilities. It is not a court, regulator, insurer or independent arbitration service. A platform complaint process does not remove rights against a supplier or WedSparks, or prevent a lawful payment-provider or external complaint.

2. Urgent concerns

If there is immediate danger, contact the relevant emergency service. For suspected fraud, account compromise or an unauthorised payment, promptly contact the appropriate account support or payment provider and take steps to protect access. Do not wait for an ordinary supplier conversation if that would increase the risk.

Keep relevant references, but do not publish another person’s private information or send passwords, authentication codes or full card details as evidence. An urgent report should clearly identify the risk, affected account or transaction and a safe contact method.

3. Start with a clear written account

For a supplier service issue, explain the concern in the booking conversation where practical. State what was agreed, what happened, the relevant date and the outcome you are seeking. Give the supplier a reasonable chance to understand and respond, unless urgency or the nature of the issue makes direct contact inappropriate.

For a platform error or credit calculation issue, identify the affected feature, payment or account record. A useful complaint is specific and factual. You do not need to surrender an external right or admit fault merely to raise a concern.

4. Keep relevant evidence

Useful records can include the accepted quote and its version, booking terms, invoices, receipts, messages, agreed changes and photographs of the issue. Explain which record supports each part of your complaint. Keep originals and avoid editing evidence in a way that changes its meaning.

Share only what is reasonably necessary. Remove unrelated guest details, health information and third-party financial data where possible. The Privacy Policy applies to platform handling of complaint information; suppliers have their own responsibilities for information they receive.

5. Describe the remedy sought

Depending on the circumstances and applicable law, a remedy might include correcting an invoice, providing missing work, agreeing a reasonable price reduction, cancelling a service, refunding money or correcting a credit balance. Explain your requested outcome and why it addresses the issue.

An advertised policy or contract condition does not displace mandatory consumer rights. Equally, a change of mind does not always create the same entitlement as a serious service failure. The parties should consider the actual agreement and events rather than assume one remedy fits every dispute.

6. Escalating to WedSparks

When the support route is configured, provide the booking or transaction reference, a concise summary, relevant documents, steps already taken and the outcome sought. Support should acknowledge the issue, identify any missing information and explain the role it can perform.

The final process must identify realistic acknowledgement and review targets, who handles conflicts of interest and how a person can seek reconsideration. This draft does not promise 24-hour support, a fixed resolution time or binding adjudication that the service cannot provide.

7. Fair participation and written outcomes

Each party should have a reasonable opportunity to present relevant information. Keep communication respectful and avoid threats, harassment or pressure to remove a truthful review as a condition of a lawful remedy. A safety restriction or fraud investigation may require some information to be withheld where legally appropriate.

Record any resolution with the amounts, currency, money and credit components, actions, responsible party and agreed timing. Confirm whether the agreement resolves all issues or only a particular part. Do not mark a complaint resolved solely because one party stops replying.

8. Card and payment-provider disputes

Your bank or payment provider may offer a transaction dispute or chargeback process with separate eligibility rules and deadlines. Check those directly and provide accurate information. An internal platform complaint does not necessarily pause a provider’s deadline or guarantee that a provider will reverse a payment.

Tell the relevant parties about related processes so duplicate refunds can be avoided. Suppliers should respond through the provider’s evidence channel where required. WedSparks must not describe a pending chargeback as a final finding about the quality of a supplier’s service.

9. External options and account action

Depending on the issue and jurisdiction, further options may include a consumer protection agency, privacy regulator, small claims tribunal, court or independent adviser. The appropriate body depends on the location and nature of the dispute. You may use applicable legal rights without first agreeing to a waiver through the platform.

Where there is credible evidence of fraud or harmful conduct, access may be restricted proportionately under the Platform Terms. A restriction should not automatically cancel valid refunds or destroy necessary records. The final support process should explain how an affected user can request a review.

10. Records, learning and changes

Complaint records may be retained where needed to administer a resolution, comply with law, defend a claim or investigate misuse. They should not be kept indefinitely without a purpose or reused for unrelated marketing. Account closure does not necessarily require deletion of records still lawfully needed for an unresolved matter.

We may improve the process as the platform develops. Material changes should be communicated appropriately and should not unfairly remove rights relating to an existing issue. This policy must be reviewed alongside the actual payment, credit and customer-support implementation before taking effect.
